agent: effects wave B - countries among each other and land changing hands
question: What the 23 diplomacy and land effects do when they run: casus_belli, change_controller, create_alliance, create_vassal, end_guarantee, end_military_access, end_non_aggression_pact, end_war, guarantee, inherit, leave_alliance, leave_faction, military_access, non_aggression_pact, relation, release, secede_province, surrender_inherit, threat, form_government_in_exile, war, undeclared_war, add_wargoal.

addresses.name: CCasusBelliEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCasusBelliEffect::Execute(CCasusBelliEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `casus_belli = TAG`: **the scope country gains a casus belli against TAG.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F4B18), 0x9A6770 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9A67DC. Resolves the tag inline (use_this: EventScope_GetCountryTag; use_from: `scope->from_country` +0x18/+0x1C read directly, not through this_scope; else `this->target` +0x20/+0x24) and calls AddCasusBelli (rva 0xE6640) with the named tag in ECX and `countries[scope->country_id]` on the stack. AddCasusBelli builds a CCasusBelli with `first` = the scope country and `second` = TAG, type 0, no end date, and CCasusBelli::Activate files it on `countries[scope]->diplomacy[TAG]->casus_belli (+0x3C)` - the list `casus_belli = TAG` the trigger reads. Nothing is checked first: a second call adds a second casus belli; only TAG == the scope country is refused (inside AddCasusBelli). An unknown tag (`---`, id 0) gives a casus belli against country 0. No message, no relation or threat change. add_casus_belli (CReversedCasusBelliEffect, 0x5A6B10) is the same call with the two parties swapped.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9A6770-0x9A67DC: `push ecx` (countries[scope+0x14]) then `lea ecx,[esp+0xc]` (resolved tag), `call 0x4E6640`. AddCasusBelli's listing writes C->tag/id into +8/+0xC and ECX's tag into +0x10/+0x14. Wrong if 0x4E6640's ECX/stack roles were the other way round - its `cmp [edi+4], [stack+0xCA8]` and the two stores settle it.

addresses.name: CChangeControllerEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CChangeControllerEffect::Execute(CChangeControllerEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `change_controller = TAG`: **TAG becomes the controller of the scope's province.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F47C4), 0x9A7DC0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9A7E9A. `Province_SetController(provinces[scope->province (+0x28)], &target, &gameState->tick, 1, 1, 0)` (rva 0xA2400), the target from Effect_ResolveCountryTarget (rva 0x5A7C30). Unguarded: on a country-scoped effect it sets the controller of **province 0**; an unknown tag makes `---` (id 0) the controller. The setter itself refuses only two things: the controller already being TAG, and, in a running game, giving control of an **unowned** province to anyone. Its other consequences (pushback damage, capital loot, rebasing air and naval units, the occupation policy, the CControllerChange history entry, area and supply regrouping because the second flag is 1) are on that entry.
addresses.evidence: Listing: pushes 0 (ebx), 1, 1, `gameState+0xBDC`, then the resolver's two arguments, then `push eax` (resolved tag) and `push esi` (province from `[gameState+0xB8C][scope+0x28]`), `call 0x4A2400`. The setter's `ret 0x18` matches six stack dwords.

addresses.name: CCreateAllianceEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCreateAllianceEffect::Execute(CCreateAllianceEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `create_alliance = TAG`: **an accepted alliance offer from the scope country to TAG, run through the ordinary diplomatic action.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F4EF4), 0x9AD7D0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9AD919. `operator new(0x28)` builds a CAllianceAction in place (vftable 0x15FB514): token 0x18D, `actor (+8)` = the scope country, `recipient (+0x10)` = TAG (Effect_ResolveCountryTarget), `type (+0x18)` = 0 then **2 = ACCEPT**, both dates the current tick, `value (+0x24)` = 1. It then calls the action's slot 7 (CAllianceAction::Apply, rva 0x618D70) and deletes it through slot 0. So create_alliance does what accepting an alliance does - the CAlliance, ALLIANCE_RELATION_CHANGE, the rebuilds and the acceptance messages - whatever that arm does; **the arm itself is not read here.** No guard in the effect for an existing alliance, the same country or country 0.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9AD8B8-0x9AD8FC: the eight stores into the new object, `mov dword ptr [esi], 0x15fb514`, `mov dword ptr [esi+0x18], 2`, `call [vft+0x1C]`, then `call [vft]` with 1. 0x15FB514 is CAllianceAction's table per its Apply entry; ACCEPT = 2 per CDiplomaticAction +0x18.

addresses.name: CCreateVassalEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCreateVassalEffect::Execute(CCreateVassalEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `create_vassal = TAG`: **TAG becomes the scope country's vassal.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F5688), 0x9B8520 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9B8593. Two gates: nothing happens if TAG is already in the scope country's `Vassals (+0xF78)` list, and nothing happens if TAG **owns no province** (`OwnedProvinces.count +0xCF8 <= 0`). Otherwise `MakeVassal(scope country, TAG)` (rva 0xD94A0, __cdecl), which is the whole of the work - see that entry. Not refused: TAG == the scope country (MakeVassal would then run on one country), or TAG already being someone else's vassal (MakeVassal deletes the old dependency).
addresses.evidence: Listing: the walk `[edx+0xF78]` comparing `[node+4]` with the resolved id, then `cmp dword ptr [eax+0xcf8], 0; jle`, then four pushes (scope tag, scope id, target tag, target id in that order of arguments) and `call 0x4D94A0; add esp, 0x10`.

addresses.name: CEndGuaranteeEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEndGuaranteeEffect::Execute(CEndGuaranteeEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `end_guarantee = TAG`: **ends the scope country's guarantee of TAG, and only that direction.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F54E4), 0x9B6590 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9B6733. With `g = countries[scope]->diplomacy[TAG]->guarantee (+0x1C)`: acts only when `g` is non-null **and** `g->first.id (+0xC) != TAG` - i.e. CDiplomacyStatus::IsGuaranting, the scope is the guarantor. Then `g`'s slot 11 (CGuarantee::Deactivate, rva 0x646E20: null +0x1C both ways, `changed` both ways), unlink from `CCurrentGameState +0xB2C relations`, delete through slot 0, and `CCountry::RebuildNeighbours` + 0xE39C0 on TAG then on the scope. A guarantee TAG gives the scope is left alone. No relation change, no influence cost, no message - unlike the revoke arm of CGuaranteeAction.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9B65E5-0x9B6604: `mov edx,[ecx+0x1c]; test; je exit; ... cmp [edx+0xc], ecx(status+0xC); je exit`, then `call [vft+0x2C]`, the relation-list walk at +0xB2C, CList_RemoveNode, `call [vft]` with 1.

addresses.comment: `end_non_aggression_pact = TAG`: when `countries[scope]->diplomacy[TAG]->nap (+0x28)` is non-null, CNap::Deactivate (slot 11, rva 0x647300 - nulls +0x28 both ways), unlink from the relation list, delete, RebuildNeighbours + 0xE39C0 on TAG and the scope. addresses.name: CEndWarEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEndWarEffect::Execute(CEndWarEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `end_war = TAG`: **takes TAG - not the scope country - and TAG's vassals out of the war the two are fighting.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F5654), 0x9B80C0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9B827E. `war = countries[scope]->diplomacy[TAG]->war (+0x20)`; null returns. TAG is looked up in `war->attackers (+0x2C..+0x30)`: found, CWar::RemoveAttacker(war, 0, TAG); otherwise CWar::RemoveDefender(war, 0, TAG) unconditionally. Then for every node of `countries[TAG]->Vassals (+0xF78)`: RemoveAttacker if the vassal is an attacker, else RemoveDefender if it is a defender, and RebuildNeighbours + 0xE39C0 + OnDiplomacyChanged on the vassal **whether or not it was in the war**. Last, RebuildNeighbours + 0xE39C0 on TAG and on the scope, OnDiplomacyChanged on the scope and on TAG. The scope country stays in the war; no peace, no war goals settled, no message.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9B810B-0x9B813E: the attackers scan compares `[eax+4]` with edi = the resolved id and both removals push edi; the vassal loop reads `[countries[edi]+0xF78]`. Wrong if the resolved id in edi were the scope's - it is `[esp+0x1c]`, the resolver's out id.

addresses.name: CGuaranteeEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGuaranteeEffect::Execute(CGuaranteeEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `guarantee = TAG`: **the scope country guarantees TAG.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F54B0), 0x9B60B0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9B62D2. Otherwise `operator new(0x28)`, CGuarantee's constructor (rva 0x646E90), `first (+8)` = the scope, `second (+0x10)` = TAG, `start_date (+0x18)` = tick, slot 10 (CGuarantee::Activate - both directions' +0x1C = this), append to the relation list (rva 0x93E10 with ESI = gameState+0xB24), RebuildNeighbours + 0xE39C0 on TAG and the scope. **If TAG already guarantees the scope it is not refused**: the new object overwrites the single +0x1C pointer both ways and the old CGuarantee stays in the relation list, unhooked. addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9B6105-0x9B6122 (the IsGuaranting test, `jne exit`), 0x9B61C4-0x9B61E8 (the four stores and `call [vft+0x28]`), 0x9B6278 (the append). CGuarantee::Activate's record: writes +0x1C both directions.

addresses.name: CInheritEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CInheritEffect::Execute(CInheritEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `inherit = TAG`: **the scope country annexes TAG** - `AnnexCountry(countries[scope], false, TAG)` (rva 0xE7B00). addresses.name: CLeaveAllianceEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLeaveAllianceEffect::Execute(CLeaveAllianceEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `leave_alliance = TAG`: ends the **bilateral** CAlliance between the scope country and TAG (`diplomacy[TAG]->alliance (+0x14)`): CAlliance::Deactivate (slot 11, rva 0x646BF0), unlink, delete, RebuildNeighbours + 0xE39C0 on both. Factions are not touched - a faction membership is not a CAlliance. No relation or influence change, no message. Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F55E8), 0x9B7930 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9B7AB8.

addresses.name: CLeaveFactionEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLeaveFactionEffect::Execute(CLeaveFactionEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `leave_faction = <faction>`: Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F4758), 0x9A21C0 to the `ret 8` at 0x9A2384 (an early `ret 8` at 0x9A2214). Nothing happens unless the scope country is in `this->faction (+0x20)`'s `Members (+0x28)`. Then, with `leader` = that list's first id (`---` when empty), it walks **every war in `CCurrentGameState +0xC00 active_war`** and removes the scope country from each war where it stands on the side whose **first-listed member is the faction leader**: in `attackers` with `attackers[0] == leader` -> CWar::RemoveAttacker(war, 0, scope); else in `defenders` with `defenders[0] == leader` -> CWar::RemoveDefender. Wars it fights on its own, or beside another leader, are kept. Then OnDiplomacyChanged(scope) and **CCountry::LeaveFaction(scope, false)** - no faction-history entry. No this/from; a misspelt faction is the null faction, whose member list the scope is not in, so nothing happens.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9A22C0-0x9A2328: per war, `cmp [eax+4], ebx` (scope id) over +0x2C..+0x30 then `cmp [esi+4], [esp+0x14]` (attackers[0] against the leader id from Members.first or 0x170CF48); the same over +0x3C..+0x40; then `push 0; call 0x4F6B20`.

addresses.name: CRelationEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRelationEffect::Execute(CRelationEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)

addresses.name: CReleaseEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CReleaseEffect::Execute(CReleaseEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `release = TAG`: **gives TAG every one of its core provinces the scope country owns.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F4C50), 0x9AA850 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9AAA73. Walks `countries[TAG]->CoreProvinces (+0xD10)` and collects each province whose `owner.id (+0x330)` is the scope country; with none collected it does nothing. Otherwise it resolves TAG a second time (same three ways), makes sure a lazy singleton at [0x1A87280] exists, and calls `ReleaseProvinces(&list, TAG)` (rva 0xC1430). TAG need not exist - this is how a dead country comes back - and TAG == the scope country is not refused (its own cores are 'released' to it). No vassal relation is created. The tag resolution is inline (use_from = `scope->from_country` directly).
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9AA8C1-0x9AA9BC: `[countries[tag.id]+0xD10]` walked, `cmp [province+0x330], scope id` before each 0x10-byte node append; `cmp dword ptr [esp+0x28], ebx; je` on the count; `push id; push tag; lea ecx,[list]; push ecx; call 0x4C1430`.

addresses.name: CSecedeProvinceEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSecedeProvinceEffect::Execute(CSecedeProvinceEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `secede_province = TAG`: **the scope's province goes to TAG if the scope country owns it.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F4BB4), 0x9A96D0 to the `ret 8` at 0x9A9A4D - and **slot 9 starts at 0x9A9A50 with no padding at all**, a new trap 2 pair. Then on `p = provinces[scope->province]`, two independent tests in this order: `p->controller == S && p->owner == TAG` -> CMapProvince::ChangeOwner(p, TAG, now, 1, 1, 0) (so occupied land of TAG's is handed back to TAG); then `p->owner == S` -> the same call (TAG takes owner and controller). addresses.name: CThreatEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CThreatEffect::Execute(CThreatEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `threat = { who = TAG value = N }`: Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F5448), 0x9B4DD0 to three `ret 8` (0x9B4E3D, 0x9B4E82, 0x9B4EC4). **With a tag**: `countries[who]->diplomacy[scope]->threat (+0x5C) += value`, floored at 0, no cap, `changed` not set - TAG feels N more threat **from the scope country**. The effect calls CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation on the scope just before and **throws the answer away**. `value` is whole numbers only (atoi x1000).
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9B4E85-0x9B4EB8: `mov ecx,[ecx+0x28]` (who id), `[countries[who]+0xE28][scope id]`, `add [eax+0x5c], edx; cmp 0; jge; mov 0`. addresses.name: CFormGovernmentInExileAction::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CFormGovernmentInExileAction::Execute(CFormGovernmentInExileAction* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `form_government_in_exile = yes`: Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F5174), 0x9BAEA0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9BB1C1; **the function above ends `ret 0x28` on the byte before the entry - no padding, a new trap 2 pair**. The host is the scope's **FROM** country. When FROM has an id: every province the scope country *controls* that lies on the continent (`CMapProvince +0x368`) of FROM's capital, or whose area borders an area FROM controls (OwnerArea_TouchesController, rva 0x7EB90), is collected, and each is handed on by Province_SetController(p, X, now, 1, 0, 0) with X = **FROM** where FROM is at war with the province's owner (or either is REB) and the province's **owner** otherwise; then the area and supply groups are rebuilt. Always, last: `SetGovernmentInExile(scope country, this->value (+0x20))` (rva 0x102BC0) - so `= no` ends an exile. With no FROM the handover is skipped and only the flag is set.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x9BAECA (`cmp [esi+0x1c], 0; je` to the tail), 0x9BAFC5/0x9BAFD9 (continent compare, `call 0x47EB90` with EAX = area +0x2B4 and ECX = scope+0x18), 0x9BB0EC-0x9BB154 (the war/REB choice and `call 0x4A2400`), 0x9BB190-0x9BB1AB (`movzx edx, byte [this+0x20]; push; push country; call 0x502BC0`). addresses.name: CWarEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWarEffect::Execute(CWarEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `war = { target = TAG limited = ... attacker_goal = {} defender_goal = {} }`: **a declaration of war run through CDeclareWarAction::Apply.** Slot 11, one holder (vftable 0x15F5844), 0x9BC6D0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x9BC993. (1) TAG from slot 12 (Effect_GetTargetCountryTag) - with no or an unknown tag, **the controller of the scope's province**. (2) If CCountry::IsEnemyTag(scope, TAG) - already at war, or either is REB - nothing happens at all, goals included. (3) Every attacker goal (vector +0x28..+0x2C, 0x2C each) gets actor = scope, recipient = TAG; every defender goal (+0x38..+0x3C) actor = TAG, recipient = scope. TAG == the scope is not refused (IsEnemyTag answers false for one country). **Child effects are not run**: no read of the child list at +8.

**CCasusBelli slot 10**, read end to end, 0xA47BB0 to the `ret` at 0xA47D00 with a second exit at 0xA47D15 (reached from 0xA47C8C). `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

One gate, on `CRelation +0x1C` (the end date): `years = (end_date - 43800000) / 24 / [0x160A550]` (365.0, truncated). **`years < 2` - no end date, the null date being the epoch itself - jumps straight to the attach** (`jl 0xA47C8E`); only a real end date is then tested, and `end_date < gameState->tick (+0xBDC)` - an expired casus belli - returns without attaching (`jl 0xA47D04`). *Corrected 2026-10-12 (FINDINGS-effectrun.md)*: this entry said `< 2` returned without doing anything, which would have made every casus belli CCasusBelli::CCasusBelli leaves undated - all of AddCasusBelli's - invisible. The first reading was reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md.

addresses.name: SpreadThreatToAll
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SpreadThreatToAll(int* amount@stack:4, int* scale@stack:8, CCountry* feared@EDI)
addresses.comment: **Threat toward `feared` felt by every other country**, the country-wide sibling of the province-graph SpreadThreat (0xF50A0). 0x4F4E80 to the single `ret 8` at 0x4F5094. `base = *amount * (1000 + feared's MODIFIER_THREAT_IMPACT (global modifier values +0x1C0)) / 1000`, **halved** when `feared->faction` is not valid (slot 7); a floor `min = base * floor(50.5f) / 1000` = a twentieth of it is kept apart. Then for every country `c` in `CCurrentGameState +0xBBC` (count from the state's slot 6) other than `feared`: `v = ThreatFactorTowards(feared, c, base)`, `v = v * (1000 - c's MODIFIER_THREAT_RESISTANCE (+0x1C8)) / 1000`, `v = max(v, min)`, and `c->diplomacy[feared]->threat (+0x5C) += *scale * v / 1000`, floored at 0. So every country gets at least a twentieth of the base, the dead ones included. Seven call sites (VAs): CThreatEffect::Execute twice (scale +1000 and -1000), CConvoy::LoseShips at 0x4C5AA1, the spy threat mission at 0x53027C, 0x4304DA, 0x430937 and 0x57DE3B.

Modifier ids 0x38/0x39 by scripts/modifierIds.py.

addresses.name: ThreatFactorTowards
addresses.signature: int* __stdcall ThreatFactorTowards(CCountry* feared, int* out, CCountryTag* other, int base) @EAX
addresses.comment: How much of `base` threat `other` feels from `feared`. 0x4FBCB0 to `ret 0x10` at 0x4FBCD1 and 0x4FBE26 (the block 0x4FBE29-0x4FBE7A is the no-faction search, jumped to and jumping back). `other->id == 0` answers 0. Otherwise: `reach = min(28 * other's OwnedProvinces count, 4000)` (map units, CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces' scale), `d` = that distance from other's acting capital (`+0xE24`) to feared's acting capital (CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation); `f = max(1000 - d * 1000 / reach, 0)`, and **1001** when `reach` is 0 (a country with no provinces); `f = 1000` outright when `other` is on feared's `Neighbours (+0xFD8)` list. `t = base * f / 1000`, then `t = t * CAlignment::GetFactionThreatDistanceFactor(&feared->alignment (+0xDC), other's faction's ideology group) / 1000` - or, when `other` is in no valid faction, the ideology group nearest **other's** own alignment (CAlignment::DistanceSquaredTo over GetIdeologies' groups whose slot 6 answers true). One caller, SpreadThreatToAll.

Inferred rather than confirmed only in what the factor means: GetFactionThreatDistanceFactor grows with ideological distance, so countries far apart in ideology feel more.

addresses.name: Province_SetController
addresses.signature: void __stdcall Province_SetController(CMapProvince* province, CCountryTag* controller, int* date, bool applyConsequences, bool rebuildAreas, bool peaceful)
addresses.comment: **The controller setter**, 24 callers. 0x4A2400 to the single `ret 0x18` at 0x4A36AE. Read from the decompilation with the listing checked at the gates; the main lines: (1) no-op when the controller is already `controller`; (2) in a running game, refuses to give control of an **unowned** province to anyone. (3) With `applyConsequences`: unless `peaceful`, when the new controller is an enemy of the old one each building (+0x310) with a level takes COMBAT_PUSHBACK_DAMAGE on a COMBAT_PUSHBACK_CHANCE_FOR_DAMAGE roll, and when the province is the old controller's acting capital a share of the old controller's stockpile ([0x1A86CEC]) goes to the new one; air units based there whose owner is an enemy of the new controller are rebased to the nearest friendly air base or removed, naval units likewise to a port; a CControllerChange history entry dated `date`. (4) The province leaves the old controller's ControlledProvinces; REB bookkeeping; the new controller's **occupation policy** toward the old is set to `civil_war` when allowed, else the first policy. (5) `controller (+0x334/+0x338)` written; an unowned province given to a non-REB gets that country as owner too (rva 0xA2180). (6) UpdateProvinceBlockaded; for a land province UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince and, with `rebuildAreas`, the area and supply groups; neighbouring owners' AI strategy flagged. (7) CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot when the controller changed, and with `applyConsequences` rva 0xE0B80 on the old controller.

addresses.name: AnnexCountry
addresses.signature: void __stdcall AnnexCountry(CCountry* annexer, bool surrender, char annexedTag[4], int annexedId)
addresses.comment: **inherit and surrender_inherit.** 0x4E7B00 to the single `ret 0x10` at 0x4E8E76, 0x1376 bytes. (1) An `ANNEX` message (ACTOR the annexer, RECIPIENT the annexed, at the annexed country's capital). (2) In surrender mode, a list of candidates: the annexed country's `non_hostile_countries (+0xF98)` less the annexer and the annexed, kept only where the annexer is at war with them (or REB is involved). (3) The annexed country leaves its faction (RemoveMember, CFaction::null, RebuildStaticModifiers, RebuildRules). (4) **For each province it owns: occupied by someone other than REB -> CMapProvince::ChangeOwner(p, its occupier, now, 1, 0, 0) - the occupier keeps it**; otherwise -> ChangeOwner(p, annexer), and in surrender mode, when a neighbouring area is controlled by a candidate (the nearest by rva 0x7E590 when several), Province_SetController(p, that candidate) after. (6) Every province it controls goes back to its owner (or, for an exiled owner in a faction, to the faction leader). (7) Area and supply groups rebuilt. (8) Every other country: out of any war with it (RemoveAttacker/RemoveDefender, flag 1), spies on it cleared, alliance, dependency and guarantee with it deleted, threat both ways reduced by 9999.000 (so to 0), trade routes deleted, rva 0x647F20. addresses.comment: **release, and release_vassal's sibling.** 0x4C1430 to the single `ret 0xC` at 0x4C21F9. `provinces` is a CList of CMapProvince*; empty does nothing. The oppressor is the first province's owner. Per province: both directions' `war_seen_tick (+0x54)` between the released country and that province's owner set to now - 24 (once per owner); **CMapProvince::ChangeOwner(p, tag, now, 1, 0, 1)**; a core for `tag` added when it has none (rva 0xA3B80); and when the province is the released country's original capital (its history's `capital` entry, else +0xE20) and its capital is elsewhere, the capital moves there (rva 0xDD730). Then area and supply groups; then **every technology the oppressor has at a higher level is raised to the oppressor's level, capped at the technology's +0x2C4**; then, when the infantry brigade type is usable (slot 9), **each released province with MODIFIER_IC > 0 spawns a CArmy of three infantry brigades** for the released country, named, at the province, with combat checked; then an `INDEPENDANCE` message (ACTOR the released, OPRESSOR the oppressor); then rva 0xF06D0(released, 1, 0). Four call sites (VAs): CReleaseEffect::Execute, 0x9AEE7D (in release_vassal's Execute), 0x4BE689 and 0x54BF32.
addresses.evidence: Listing for the IC test (`mov eax,[esi+0x114]; cmp dword ptr [eax+0x78], ebx` at 0x4C1892 - modifier id 15, MODIFIER_IC, trap 5) and the exit; the rest from the decompilation.

addresses.name: SetGovernmentInExile
addresses.signature: void __stdcall SetGovernmentInExile(CCountry* country, bool inExile)
addresses.comment: Bounded by wave 15 (0x502BC0 to the `ret 8` at 0x5033AD; four `ret 8` arms) and named now. `inExile` = 1: a country already in exile only has the flag re-set; otherwise `+0xA08` = 0, `government_in_exile (+0x95)` = 1, **Manpower (+0xBCC) and officers (+0xC4) multiplied by floor(100.5f)/1000 - cut to a tenth**, the +0xF40 list destroyed, every unit standing on ground whose controller is not a friend (CCountry::IsFriend) removed - or, for an expeditionary unit, handed back (rva 0x1020E0, ShatterUnit) - the faction-leader promotion already recorded as FactionLeaderPromotion (rva 0x102F34), the acting capital moved toward the faction leader's (rva 0xDD670) when it is not the leader, and, when the acting capital is no longer its own, **every trade route of the country deleted**. `inExile` = 0: when in exile, land regiments with supply consumption below 1 are converted by a defines-named type (rva 0x1ABDD0), units rebuilt, acting capital = declared capital, flag cleared. Any other value is stored as the flag. Seven callers including CFormGovernmentInExileAction::Execute.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; [0x160A684] = 100.5f read from the image; the `cmp [ebp+0xC], 1` at 0x502BE6 is wave 15's. Inferred: read from the decompilation, not instruction by instruction.
